intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unforgettable experience. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the breathtaking scenery.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Interact with local vendors and learn about Greek culinary traditions and ingredients.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Elafonissi Beach on Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade through the warm, shallow waters to the small island, sunbathe on the unique pink sand, and enjoy the natural beauty of one of Europe's most exotic beaches.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Crete to learn how to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades (honey donuts). Visit a local market beforehand to select fresh ingredients, and enjoy your meal with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Hopping by ATV
experiences.description: Rent an ATV and explore Mykonos's best beaches at your own pace. Visit Paradise Beach, Super Paradise Beach, and Elia Beach — each offering crystal-clear Aegean waters, golden sand, and a lively atmosphere. Stop at local beach tavernas to try fresh grilled octopus, Greek salad, and fresh fish by the sea.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and clear customs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget bus or shared taxi from the airport to Zakynthos Town port, then catch the ferry or local transfer to Navagio Beach area. Check in to the Boutique Stay and freshen up. Take a short stroll along the cliffside paths near Navagio for stunning first views of the famous Shipwreck Beach from above.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the accommodation and explore the nearest village on foot. Find a local taverna for a relaxed first dinner and a cold Greek beer.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap or gyros from a street kiosk near the port in Zakynthos Town (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Local taverna near accommodation — try grilled sardines, Greek salad and house wine (€10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities only begin after 13:00 arrival. Pre-book ferry or shared transfer in advance to save money. Keep energy for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat trip from the nearby cove down to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach — the most iconic beach in Greece. Arrive before the crowds for calm turquoise waters and dramatic white cliffs. Swim and snorkel around the rusted shipwreck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by boat and walk the cliffside trail above Navagio for panoramic photography. Visit the free cliff viewpoint platform. Pack a homemade picnic from the local mini-market to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearby village of Anafonitria for a quiet evening walk. Visit the 15th-century Anafonitria Monastery (free entry). Return to accommodation for a light meal.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local bakery (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the cliffs — fresh bread, local cheese (graviera), olives and tomatoes from the mini-market (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation or grab takeaway spanakopita and tiropita from a local bakery (€4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip to Navagio Beach the evening before — group boat tours are the most budget-friendly option (€10–15 per person). Go early to beat the midday heat and tourist rush.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or bicycle from a local rental shop to explore the northwestern coast of Zakynthos independently. Ride down to Porto Vromi, a sheltered cove with crystal-clear water — perfect for morning swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the coastal ride to the Blue Caves near Cape Skinari on the northern tip of the island. Take a small rowboat tour into the caves to see the electric-blue water reflections (affordable local boat operators charge €5–8). Swim in the sea nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Ride back south and stop in the village of Volimes, known for its local honey, nougat and handmade crafts. Sample free tastings at roadside stalls. Return to accommodation before sunset.

meals.breakfast: Freshly baked koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee at a village kafeneio (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled octopus and bread at a small seaside café near Porto Vromi (€8–10)
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek moussaka and house salad at a family-run taverna in Anafonitria village (€9–12)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs approximately €15–20 per day. Wear sunscreen and bring a water bottle. The Blue Caves are best visited in the morning when sunlight creates the most vivid blue reflections.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Zakynthos Town (Chora). Visit the free Byzantine Museum in Solomos Square to see icons and religious art salvaged from the 1953 earthquake. Walk through the neoclassical town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Zakynthos Town's waterfront promenade (Strata Marina). Visit the Venetian Castle on the hill above town (€3 entry) for sweeping views over the Ionian Sea. Walk through the castle ruins and enjoy the breeze.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively backstreets of Zakynthos Town for dinner. The area around Agios Markos Square has many affordable local restaurants. Try a full traditional Greek mezze spread shared between travelers.

meals.breakfast: Cheese pie (tiropita) and Greek coffee at a bakery in Zakynthos Town (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh calamari and tzatziki with pita at a harbour-side ouzeri (€8–11)
meals.dinner: Mezze dinner — dolmades, taramasalata, grilled halloumi, and village bread at a local taverna (€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The local KTEL bus from the Navagio area to Zakynthos Town is very affordable (€2–3 each way). The Byzantine Museum is free on certain national holidays — check in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Gerakas Beach on the southeastern tip of Zakynthos — one of the most beautiful and ecologically protected beaches on the island. Swim in calm, shallow turquoise water. This beach is a nesting site for Caretta caretta sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the nature trail along the dunes at Gerakas. Visit the free Sea Turtle Information Center run by ARCHELON volunteers. Relax on the beach through the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the village of Vasilikos on the way back for a sunset drink at a beachside café. Return to accommodation via local bus or shared taxi.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with fresh seasonal fruit at the accommodation (self-prepared, €2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the mini-market — hummus, pita, cucumber and cherry tomatoes (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Fresh fish of the day at a simple seaside taverna in Vasilikos village (€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has restricted access after sunset to protect turtle nesting — respect all signs. Bring your own snorkeling gear if possible to avoid rental costs. Reachable by local bus or scooter.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Zakynthos port to Kefalonia (Pessada or Argostoli port). Arrive and rent a bicycle or use local buses to begin exploring. Head to Myrtos Beach — one of the most dramatic beaches in the Ionian Islands with white pebbles and vivid blue water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Myrtos and hike the short trail to the viewpoint above the beach for spectacular aerial photos. Continue to the nearby village of Divarata for a rest and cold drink.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Argostoli, the capital of Kefalonia. Walk the waterfront promenade and watch the famous Kefalonian loggerhead turtles that gather near the port at dusk. Find budget accommodation in Argostoli for the night.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and bougatsa (custard pastry) at a café near Zakynthos port before the ferry (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks at Myrtos Beach — local cheese, bread and fruit (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) and local Robola wine at a traditional restaurant in Argostoli (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry from Zakynthos to Kefalonia (Pessada) costs approximately €8–12 per person. Book in advance during June. This is a travel day so keep luggage light and manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Drogarati Cave near Sami — a stunning natural limestone cave with impressive stalactites and stalagmites (€5 entry). The cave maintains a cool temperature, a welcome relief from the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Melissani Lake Cave nearby — a unique underground lake where sunlight pierces through the collapsed roof to create magical turquoise reflections. Take the short rowboat tour (€7). Swim at Antisamos Beach afterward, the lush green bay used in the film Captain Corelli's Mandolin.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Argostoli for the evening. Stroll through the central market and pick up local products. Enjoy dinner in a busy local square.

meals.breakfast: Bread, local honey and coffee at the accommodation or a nearby café (€3)
meals.lunch: Grilled fresh fish and Greek salad at a simple taverna near Sami port (€10–13)
meals.dinner: Stuffed peppers with rice and minced meat (gemista) at a family taverna in Argostoli (€8–11)

day_by_day.notes: Drogarati Cave and Melissani Lake are close together — visit both in the same afternoon to save on transport. Antisamos Beach is a short drive from Sami and is less crowded than other beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Kefalonia (Sami or Patra connection) or a combination of ferry and bus toward Athens. Alternatively, fly with a short domestic flight if budget allows. Arrive in Athens and check in to a budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psyrri neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Monastiraki Flea Market — a labyrinth of stalls selling antiques, vintage clothing and local goods. Browse freely (no entry cost). Explore the surrounding streets of Psyrri and Thissio.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up to the Acropolis Hill area at sunset for free exterior views of the Parthenon silhouette. The Filopappou Hill viewpoint is free and offers equally stunning panoramic views of Athens.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a koulouri from a street vendor near the ferry port (€2)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki and tzatziki wrap from a street grill in Monastiraki — Athens' most famous budget food (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Traditional Athenian taverna in Psyrri — lamb chops, tzatziki and village salad (€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel day between islands and Athens. Budget for ferry and/or bus costs (€20–35 depending on route). Monastiraki and Psyrri are ideal budget-friendly neighborhoods with great food and atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis of Athens and the Parthenon (€20 entry, or free with EU student card). Arrive at opening time (08:00) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Erechtheion, the Temple of Athena Nike and the Propylaea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill (€10 entry) — one of the finest archaeological museums in the world with original Parthenon sculptures. Walk through the Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district with charming neoclassical streets.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Plaka or Monastiraki. Watch the sunset from the rooftop terrace of a café with Acropolis views (many offer free viewpoints with a drink purchase).

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and tiropita at a Plaka bakery (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch at a Plaka taverna — shared plates of dips, olives and grilled vegetables (€8–10)
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus, fava bean dip and ouzo at an ouzeri in Monastiraki (€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: The combined ticket for the Acropolis and surrounding archaeological sites (€30) gives access to multiple sites and is better value if you plan to visit more than one. Free entry on the first Sunday of each month November–March (not applicable in June).

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Piraeus port and catch an early ferry to the island of Aegina — just 35–40 minutes away and very affordable (€8–10 return). Explore Aegina Town's colorful harbour filled with pistachio stalls and fishing boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (€5–8) or take a local bus to the Temple of Aphaia — a remarkably preserved ancient Doric temple with sea views (€6 entry). Stop at a pistachio farm roadside stall — Aegina is famous for the best pistachios in Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Piraeus and head back into Athens. Relax in Thissio neighborhood with a coffee overlooking the ancient Agora.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and coffee on the ferry or at Piraeus port (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Grilled fresh fish at a simple harbour-front taverna in Aegina Town (€10–13)
meals.dinner: Affordable souvlaki dinner back in Athens — mixed grill plate with pita and fries (€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is an excellent budget day trip from Athens — very easy and cheap to reach. Buy a bag of Aegina pistachios to take home as a delicious souvenir. Return ferry times run until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a KTEL bus from Athens to Cape Sounion (€6–7 each way, about 1.5 hours). Visit the Temple of Poseidon perched dramatically on a cliff above the Aegean Sea (€8 entry). Explore the ruins and enjoy the breathtaking coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the small beach below Cape Sounion or at Legrena Beach nearby — a quieter, local spot with clean water. Relax and soak up the sun before returning to Athens.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale but walkable neighborhood of Kolonaki in Athens. Window shop along Tsakalof Street and find a budget-friendly neighborhood taverna for dinner away from the tourist trail.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at the hostel or a nearby café (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Cape Sounion — bread, local cheese, olives and cold water (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Home-style Greek cooking at a neighborhood taverna in Pangrati or Koukaki district — stuffed vine leaves and roast lamb (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus to Cape Sounion departs from the Mavromateon Street terminal in Athens. Go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. The sunset at the Temple of Poseidon is legendary — time your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the Acropolis combined ticket or €10 separately) — the heart of ancient Athenian democracy. See the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Archaeological Museum of Athens (€10 entry) — the most important archaeological museum in Greece with treasures from across the ancient world including the Antikythera Mechanism and Minoan frescoes.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — stroll through the vibrant Exarchia neighborhood for a local, bohemian atmosphere. Visit a traditional ouzeri for a farewell mezze spread with ouzo or tsipouro.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa with cream filling and a freddo espresso at a central Athens café (€4–5)
meals.lunch: Cheap and cheerful gyros plate with fries at a local grill near Omonia Square (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Full mezze farewell dinner — assorted dips, grilled seafood, village sausages and local wine at an Exarchia ouzeri (€13–16)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is a full half-day experience — arrive early to enjoy it without rushing. Exarchia is safe and very local — a great way to experience authentic Athenian neighborhood life away from tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — pack and check out of accommodation. If time allows before departure, grab a last Greek coffee and a sesame koulouri from a street vendor. Visit the nearby Central Market (Varvakios Agora) for a final sensory experience of Greek produce, spices and local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) via the affordable metro X95 express bus (€6) or metro line 3 (€9). Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for last-minute Greek olive oil, honey or herbs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Greek beaches, ancient history and unforgettable local food.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri with sesame and a Greek coffee from a street cart near the accommodation (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Final souvlaki wrap or spanakopita at the airport or nearby (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — pick up snacks at a duty-free shop

day_by_day.notes: Keep airport transfer time generous — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. The Athens metro to the airport is reliable and budget-friendly. A perfect final memory: sip a last Greek coffee while watching the city from the airport terrace.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Zakynthos Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Zakynthos Airport to Boutique Stay near Navagio Beach (approx. 45–60 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the local area to get your bearings. Enjoy your first views of the stunning Ionian coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and head to a nearby taverna in the Anafonitria village area for a relaxed welcome dinner. Sip local Verdea white wine and watch the sunset over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: On the plane / airport snack
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside café en route to the hotel
meals.dinner: Taverna Navagio or a local village taverna near Anafonitria — try grilled octopus, horiatiki (Greek salad), and fresh bread. Budget approx. €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 13:00 arrival. Keep the evening light to recover from travel. Confirm hotel transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic boat trip from Porto Vromi (15 min drive from hotel) to Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) — one of Greece's most photographed spots. Arrive early (9:00–10:00) before the crowds. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the famous rusted shipwreck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Porto Vromi by boat and visit the nearby Blue Caves along the northern coast — a series of stunning sea caves with electric-blue water. Many boat tours combine both stops. Spend time snorkeling in the caves.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the village of Volimes (20 min) — a traditional hilltop village known for local honey, textiles, and cheese. Browse small artisan shops before returning for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique hotel or a local café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab sandwiches from a local bakery to enjoy on the beach at Navagio.
meals.dinner: Taverna in Volimes village — try lamb kleftiko, tzatziki, and spanakopita. Approx. €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Navagio boat trip in advance during June — it fills up quickly. Wear reef-safe sunscreen. Bring cash for boat operators.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Venetian Castle of Zakynthos (Kastro) ruins above Bochali village (approx. 1 hr drive south). Explore the Byzantine ruins and enjoy panoramic views over Zakynthos Town and the Ionian Sea. The morning light is perfect for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) waterfront. Stroll along the Solomos Square, visit the Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians, and browse the neoclassical architecture rebuilt after the 1953 earthquake.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Zakynthos Town's lively harbor area. The town has excellent mid-range seafood restaurants along the marina.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local kafeneion — Greek coffee, koulouri (sesame bread ring), and tiropita (cheese pie).
meals.lunch: Seaside café in Zakynthos Town — try fresh grilled fish of the day with a glass of ouzo. Approx. €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant near the marina in Zakynthos Town — order bourdeto (spicy fish stew, a Zakynthos specialty) or fresh lobster pasta. Approx. €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Town is about 40–50 min drive from Navagio area. Consider combining with grocery shopping for snacks. Free entry to castle ruins.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the quieter northern beaches of Zakynthos — visit Makris Gialos and Xigia Beach (sulfur springs beach, approx. 20 min drive). The natural sulfur springs at Xigia are said to have therapeutic properties. Swim and relax on the pebble beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the scenic northern coastal road and stop at the Cape Skinari lighthouse. Take a kayak or paddleboard rental from a local operator near the cape and paddle along the dramatic limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Navagio area and enjoy sundowners at a clifftop bar or viewpoint overlooking Navagio Bay — one of the world's most spectacular sunset views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs, local cheese, olives, fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Fish taverna near Xigia Beach or Cape Skinari — grilled sea bream, Greek salad, and local wine. Approx. €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Back near the hotel — try a local family-run taverna for moussaka, gemista (stuffed tomatoes), and house wine. Approx. €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Xigia Beach has a strong sulfur smell — perfectly normal and harmless. Bring water shoes for pebble beaches. Sunset viewpoint at Navagio cliffs is free but gets busy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Zakynthos Port (Skinari or Agios Nikolaos) to Kefalonia island (approx. 1–1.5 hr crossing). Arrive in Pesada or Poros and drive to Myrtos Beach — one of Greece's most stunning beaches with dramatic white pebbles and vivid blue water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Assos village — a charming, colorful fishing village on a narrow peninsula with a Venetian castle. Walk up to the castle ruins and swim in the sheltered cove below.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Fiskardo — Kefalonia's most picturesque and upscale harbor village, spared by the 1953 earthquake. Browse the waterfront, enjoy cocktails at a harbor bar, and have dinner before the return ferry.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — yogurt, honey, toast.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna near Myrtos — fresh calamari, dakos salad, and cold Mythos beer. Approx. €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant in Fiskardo — try Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) or fresh lobster with pasta. Approx. €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day trip — depart early (7:30–8:00). Book ferry tickets in advance. Rent a car on Kefalonia or arrange a day-tour from Zakynthos. Return ferry in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a morning swim at a nearby quiet cove accessible from the Navagio area. Read, relax, and recharge after the previous day's excursion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Anafonitria Monastery (5 min drive) — a 15th-century monastery associated with Saint Dionysios, patron saint of Zakynthos. Peaceful, beautiful, and free to visit. Then explore the surrounding olive groves and countryside on a short walk.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking experience or wine tasting: Look for a local agritourism farm or winery near the Volimes/Anafonitria area offering evening tastings of local Verdea wine and Zakynthos olive oil with mezedes (small plates).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — fresh pastries, local honey, Greek yogurt, fruit.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel terrace or nearby café — bruschetta with local tomatoes, halloumi, and cold drinks.
meals.dinner: Wine and food tasting evening at a local winery or agritourism estate — mezedes spread including local cheeses, cured meats, olives, and dips. Approx. €25–35 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: A deliberate slower day to balance the trip. Check with hotel for recommended local wineries or farm experiences — many operate informally and are best booked through local contacts.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour to the Keri Caves and Marathonisi Island (Turtle Island) in the south of Zakynthos (approx. 1 hr drive, then boat). Marathonisi is a protected nesting site for loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta). Swim and snorkel in the protected bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Keri Village and the Keri Lighthouse at the southwestern tip of the island. Dramatic cliff views, a charming village square, and a local taverna make this a perfect afternoon stop. Explore the tar springs of Keri — historically used to seal ancient ships.
day_by_day.evening: Return north and stop at Laganas Bay area for a walk along the beach promenade. Laganas is lively in the evening — good for a casual drink and people-watching before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs your way, local bread, coffee.
meals.lunch: Taverna in Keri Village — try local specialties like stifado (slow-cooked stew) or grilled lamb chops with roasted potatoes. Approx. €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Casual seafood restaurant in Laganas area — fresh mussels, calamari, and a Greek salad. Approx. €18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Turtle nesting season is June–August — do not disturb nests or turtles. Swimming near Marathonisi is allowed in designated areas. Book the boat tour from Keri port.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a ferry from Zakynthos to Athens (flight approx. 1 hr, or ferry + bus approx. 6–7 hrs — flight recommended). Arrive in Athens and check in to a mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon — Greece's most iconic landmark. Go in the afternoon (after 15:00) when crowds thin slightly. Explore the Propylaea, Erechtheion, and the Temple of Athena Nike. Views over Athens are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest neighborhood with charming neoclassical buildings, bougainvillea-draped streets, and excellent tavernas. Browse souvenir shops and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near Zakynthos hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Light meal near the Acropolis — grab a souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk (€3–4) or sit down at a café in Monastiraki. Approx. €8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Plaka — try pastitsio (Greek lasagna), grilled lamb, and baklava for dessert. Approx. €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online in advance — queues can be very long in June. Acropolis entry approx. €20. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis Museum (open from 9:00) — world-class museum housing original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis. Spend 2–3 hours exploring. The glass floor revealing ancient ruins beneath is remarkable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ancient Agora of Athens and the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Walk through Monastiraki Flea Market — great for browsing antiques, vintage items, and local crafts. Head up to Anafiotika — a hidden Cycladic-style neighborhood on the slopes of the Acropolis Hill.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar experience in Athens — many hotels and bars near Monastiraki offer stunning Acropolis views at sunset. Then dinner in the trendy Koukaki or Psyrri neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel — Greek coffee (ellinikos), tiropita, and fresh orange juice. Approx. €6–9 per person.
meals.lunch: Monastiraki street food — souvlaki, gyros wrap, or spanakopita from a local bakery. Approx. €5–10 per person.
meals.dinner: Modern Greek restaurant in Psyrri — try creative mezedes like fava bean dip, saganaki (fried cheese), grilled octopus, and local craft beer. Approx. €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Acropolis Museum entry approx. €15. The flea market is most lively on Sunday mornings. Psyrri is Athens' bohemian neighborhood — great for nightlife if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion (70 km south of Athens, 1.5 hr by bus or car). Visit the Temple of Poseidon perched dramatically on a cliff 60 m above the Aegean Sea. Lord Byron famously carved his name here. Stunning morning light and relatively few crowds early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at one of the beaches along the Athens Riviera on the return journey — Vouliagmeni Lake (thermal lake) or Varkiza Beach are excellent choices. Swim, sunbathe, and relax in the warm Aegean waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens. Dinner in the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood or near Syntagma Square. Explore Lycabettus Hill at dusk for panoramic night views over Athens (funicular or 20-min hike).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab pastries from a local bakery before departure.
meals.lunch: Seafood taverna near Cape Sounion or along the Riviera — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and Greek salad with sea views. Approx. €20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Bistro or taverna in Kolonaki — try dakos, grilled sea bass, and loukoumades (honey donuts) for dessert. Approx. €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Temple of Poseidon entry approx. €10. KTEL buses run regularly from Athens to Sounion (approx. €7 each way). Vouliagmeni Lake has an entry fee of approx. €15 but is worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Take a high-speed ferry from Piraeus Port to Hydra Island (approx. 1.5 hrs). Hydra is a car-free island of extraordinary beauty — donkeys are the main transport. Explore the charming port town, the stone mansions, and the narrow alleyways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a donkey ride to one of Hydra's quieter beaches — Vlychos or Bisti Beach. Swim in the clear Aegean waters and enjoy the island's peaceful atmosphere. Hydra has a wonderful artistic heritage — many artists have lived here.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at a waterfront restaurant in Hydra port before the return ferry. The port is magical in the evening with candlelit tavernas and the sound of the sea.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Piraeus before ferry — Greek yogurt, honey, coffee.
meals.lunch: Taverna on the waterfront in Hydra Town — try fresh grilled octopus, white bean soup, and local wine. Approx. €20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Candlelit waterfront restaurant in Hydra port — fresh catch of the day, lobster pasta, or lamb chops. Approx. €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hydrofoil/ferry tickets approx. €35–45 each way — book in advance. No cars on Hydra — embrace the slow pace. Bring cash as some smaller establishments don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final full morning in Athens. Visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) — see the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold artifacts, and ancient sculptures. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street — Athens' vibrant covered market with stalls of fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local produce. A feast for the senses. Pick up local food souvenirs: olive oil, saffron, thyme honey, and dried herbs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views — splurge slightly for the final night. Many excellent options in the Monastiraki and Thissio areas offer both great food and unforgettable views.

meals.breakfast: Slow hotel breakfast — enjoy every last bite of Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Mezedopoleio (mezedes restaurant) near the Central Market — a spread of small plates including taramosalata, dolmades, gigantes beans, and grilled halloumi. Approx. €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Monastiraki/Thissio with Acropolis views — splurge on a tasting menu or order grilled lamb, fresh seafood, and Greek wine. Approx. €35–50 per person for the final night.

day_by_day.notes: National Archaeological Museum entry approx. €12. Central Market is closed on Sundays. Book the farewell dinner rooftop restaurant in advance — they fill up fast in June.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — depending on your departure flight time. If time allows, enjoy a last Greek coffee at a café in Monastiraki Square, watching the city wake up. Visit any last-minute souvenir shops or pick up local food gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos). Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before departure. Enjoy a final Greek meal at the airport if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home memories of turquoise waters, ancient ruins, fresh seafood, and the warmth of Greek hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a Monastiraki café — freddo espresso or Greek coffee, bougatsa (custard pastry), and fresh fruit. Approx. €8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — souvlaki wrap or a Greek salad. Approx. €10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. Athens Metro Line 3 connects the city center directly to the airport (approx. 40 min, €10). Keep some euros for last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Zakynthos International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique stay at Navagio Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Zakynthos Airport to your boutique stay near Navagio Beach. Check in, unpack, and settle into your clifftop suite. Enjoy a welcome drink on your private terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea. Take a leisurely stroll along the clifftop viewpoint for your first breathtaking look at the iconic Shipwreck Beach (Navagio) below.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel's infinity pool as the sun sets over the Ionian Sea. Enjoy a curated welcome cocktail from the in-house mixologist before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light mezze platter and fresh fruit welcome spread prepared by the boutique hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium clifftop restaurant near Porto Vromi — try fresh-caught sea bream (tsipoura) grilled with lemon and herbs, paired with a crisp Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00. Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Navagio Beach is only accessible by boat — no activities at the beach itself on arrival day. Keep the evening relaxed after travel.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion to Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) — depart from Porto Vromi Marina at 09:00 before the crowds arrive. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous shipwreck up close. Snorkeling equipment provided on the private charter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat tour along the Blue Caves (Sykia and Keri Caves) on the northern coast of Zakynthos. The afternoon light creates stunning blue reflections inside the sea caves. Swim in secluded coves only accessible by boat. Return to Porto Vromi Marina by 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique hotel for a sunset aperitivo on your private terrace. Freshly prepared local cheese and charcuterie board with Zakynthian specialties including ladotyri cheese and local olives.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast on your private terrace — Greek yogurt with Zakynthian honey and walnuts, fresh pastries, eggs prepared to order, fresh orange juice and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the hotel chef, enjoyed aboard the private boat — sourdough sandwiches with local graviera cheese, prosciutto, heirloom tomatoes, fresh fruit, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at a renowned seafood taverna in the Porto Vromi area — whole lobster pasta (astakomakaronada) and grilled octopus with capers, accompanied by local Verdea white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2 days in advance. Depart early (09:00) to enjoy Navagio Beach before day-trip boats arrive. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes. Sea temperature approximately 24–25°C — ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep tour of the rugged northern Zakynthos landscape. Explore the dramatic limestone cliffs, hidden viewpoints above Navagio Beach, and the scenic village of Anafonitria. Visit the 15th-century Monastery of Anafonitria, the oldest surviving monastery on the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the traditional hilltop village of Volimes, known for its local honey, handmade lace, and artisan products. Browse premium local shops and taste Zakynthian honey varieties directly from local producers. Continue to the panoramic viewpoint at Cape Skinari for sweeping Ionian Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-suite dining experience — the hotel chef prepares a curated 4-course tasting menu featuring exclusively local Zakynthian ingredients on your terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked salmon on toasted village bread, soft-boiled eggs, fresh seasonal fruit platter, Greek coffee and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a family-run taverna in Volimes village — slow-cooked lamb with kritharaki (orzo pasta), village salad with local feta, and fresh-baked bread with olive oil
meals.dinner: Private in-suite 4-course chef's menu: (1) Amuse-bouche of smoked roe (taramosalata) on crispy phyllo, (2) Grilled calamari with lemon vinaigrette, (3) Slow-braised Zakynthian goat with roasted vegetables and herbs, (4) Loukoumades (honey donuts) with Zakynthian thyme honey and crushed pistachios

day_by_day.notes: The jeep tour offers access to viewpoints not reachable by regular vehicles. Wear comfortable shoes for monastery visits. The private chef dinner should be arranged with the hotel concierge at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking session along the dramatic limestone coastline near Navagio Beach — depart at 07:00 for calm morning seas. Paddle through sea arches and into hidden grottos with a private guide. Return by 09:30 for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon at the hotel's infinity pool and private sunbathing terrace. Optional: book a 90-minute traditional Greek aromatherapy massage and body treatment at the hotel's spa using local olive oil and herbs.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing cruise aboard a luxury catamaran departing from Porto Vromi. Sail along the western coast of Zakynthos as the sun sets dramatically into the Ionian Sea. Champagne and canapés served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Post-kayaking gourmet breakfast at the hotel — avocado toast with poached eggs and local microgreens, freshly squeezed pomegranate juice, Greek yogurt parfait, and specialty cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled halloumi salad with watermelon and mint, chilled gazpacho, and a fresh seafood ceviche with Ionian herbs
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the catamaran or at a premium waterfront restaurant in Porto Vromi — grilled whole fish of the day (catch dependent), stuffed vine leaves (dolmades) with avgolemono sauce, and a fine selection of Greek island wines

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking is best at sunrise when seas are calmest — bring a waterproof bag for your phone and camera. The sunset sailing cruise typically lasts 2–2.5 hours. Book the spa treatment and catamaran in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) — approximately 40 minutes. Explore the elegant Venetian-influenced capital. Visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos featuring remarkable post-Byzantine icons and frescoes rescued from destroyed churches. Walk through the grand Plateia Solomou (Solomos Square) and visit the neoclassical Church of Saint Dionysios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming backstreets and local markets of Zakynthos Town. Visit a premium local deli to sample and purchase Zakynthian specialties: mandola almond sweets, pasteli sesame bars, local olive oils, and the famous Zakynthian nougat (mandolato). Stroll along the picturesque harbor promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zakynthos Town before private transfer back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — traditional Greek spanakopita (spinach pie), fresh pastries, local cheeses and cold cuts, freshly squeezed orange juice, and Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a refined restaurant in Zakynthos Town — sofrito (Zakynthian veal in white wine and garlic sauce), a signature local dish, with village bread and a glass of local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of Zakynthos Town's finest restaurants — kakavia (traditional Greek fisherman's soup) followed by grilled red mullet (barbounia) with capers and lemon, and a dessert of galaktoboureko (custard pastry with syrup)

day_by_day.notes: Sofrito is the iconic dish of Zakynthos and must be tried in town. The Byzantine Museum is closed on Mondays — check ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the town exploration. Purchase mandolato as a premium local gift or treat.

day_by_day.morning: Full leisure morning at Navagio Beach — take the private hotel boat transfer down to the beach at 08:30 before the crowds. Spend the morning swimming, sunbathing on the white pebble beach, and exploring the famous rusted shipwreck (MV Panagiotis). Bring snorkeling gear for underwater exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel by private boat at 13:00. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the hotel's clifftop infinity pool with panoramic views. Optional: private yoga session on the terrace arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dining setup on the clifftop edge — the hotel arranges a romantic candlelit table at the cliff viewpoint above Navagio Beach with a 5-course tasting menu and sommelier-curated wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before beach departure — Greek yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, and pastries with coffee to go
meals.lunch: Beach picnic basket from the hotel chef — fresh baguettes, local cheeses, cured meats, marinated olives, and chilled sparkling water and rosé
meals.dinner: 5-course clifftop tasting menu: (1) Oysters with ouzo mignonette, (2) Grilled prawn bisque with saffron cream, (3) Pan-seared sea bass with fennel and citrus, (4) Lamb rack with herb crust and roasted root vegetables, (5) Dark chocolate and olive oil mousse with sea salt — paired with curated Greek wines throughout

day_by_day.notes: The clifftop private dining experience must be booked well in advance and is weather dependent. This is the most iconic beach in Greece — arriving early (08:30) is essential to experience it before the day-tripper boats arrive at 10:00–11:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to the southern part of Zakynthos — visit the Keri Lighthouse at the island's southern tip for panoramic views. Explore the Keri wetlands, a protected Natura 2000 area where Mediterranean loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) nest. Guided nature walk with a local naturalist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the beautiful Gerakas Beach in the south — a protected turtle nesting beach with golden sand and clear water. Swim and relax (swimming is permitted in designated areas away from nesting zones). Continue to Banana Beach for a more vibrant beach club experience with premium sun loungers.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the charming village of Argassi or Laganas before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit bowl, warm croissants with local honey and butter, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch at Banana Beach — fresh seafood platters, grilled vegetables with tzatziki, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a refined southern Zakynthos restaurant — moussaka prepared with premium local ingredients, grilled swordfish (xifias) steaks with capers and olives, and local dessert of revani (semolina cake with syrup)

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has strict rules to protect turtle nesting — no umbrellas or sun loungers in certain sections, and the beach closes at sunset. Respect all wildlife protection guidelines. The southern Zakynthos landscape is notably different from the dramatic north — lush and green.

day_by_day.morning: Private premium cooking class with a local Zakynthian chef — held at a traditional farmhouse near the village of Machairado. Learn to prepare authentic Zakynthian dishes: sofrito, pastitsada, and mandolato sweets using locally sourced ingredients including olive oil, herbs, and fresh produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Monastery of Saint George of the Kremnos (Agios Georgios Krimnon) — a 16th-century clifftop monastery with spectacular coastal views. Explore the surrounding countryside and olive groves. Optional: visit a premium local olive oil producer for a tasting and tour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Enjoy the dishes prepared during the morning cooking class served as a private dinner on your terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — traditional tiropita (cheese pie), local yogurt with Zakynthian honey, seasonal fruit, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the cooking class farmhouse — enjoy the dishes you prepared: sofrito, village salad, fresh bread, and local wine
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner with the remaining dishes from the cooking class, complemented by a premium bottle of Zakynthian Verdea wine and a dessert of the homemade mandolato prepared during the class

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class runs approximately 3–4 hours including preparation, cooking, and eating. Book through the hotel concierge. The olive oil tasting at a local producer is a wonderful way to understand Zakynthian agricultural heritage — purchase premium extra virgin olive oil to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the hotel — sleep in and enjoy a late breakfast on your terrace. Spend the morning relaxing at the infinity pool with views over the Ionian Sea. Optional: 60-minute hot stone massage at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion to the secluded Marathonisi Island (Turtle Island) in the Laganas Bay — a protected sea turtle habitat. Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters and look for sea turtles in their natural environment with a certified marine guide. Swim in the island's pristine sandy cove.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the hotel bar — ask the mixologist to create a signature cocktail using local Zakynthian ingredients (kumquat liqueur, local honey, fresh citrus). Watch the sunset from the clifftop.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late hotel breakfast — full Greek spread with local cheeses, honey, olives, eggs any style, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on Marathonisi Island — prepared by the hotel: chilled seafood, artisan bread, premium cheeses, and chilled sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant with sea views near Porto Vromi — grilled langoustines with garlic butter, seafood risotto with local herbs, and a fine Santorini Assyrtiko wine

day_by_day.notes: Marathonisi is a protected area — no littering and no touching the sea turtles if encountered. The marine guide will brief you on responsible wildlife watching. This is one of the best opportunities to see Caretta caretta sea turtles in Greece.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the nearby island of Kefalonia — depart by private speedboat from Porto Vromi at 08:00 (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Explore the stunning Myrtos Beach, consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in Europe, with dramatic white cliffs and vivid blue water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Venetian town of Assos on Kefalonia — a picturesque peninsula village with a Venetian castle. Walk through the village, enjoy the harbor, and explore the castle ruins with panoramic views. Optional: visit the famous Melissani Lake cave — a collapsed cave with an underground lake where sunlight creates magical blue reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Private speedboat return to Zakynthos arriving approximately 19:30. Dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — energy-boosting spread of eggs, pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a clifftop restaurant in Assos, Kefalonia — fresh Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), local lobster, and a glass of Robola white wine (Kefalonia's signature grape)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel restaurant upon return — lighter evening meal of fresh Greek salad, grilled sea bream, and a glass of chilled rosé

day_by_day.notes: The private speedboat to Kefalonia should be arranged through a licensed charter company — book at least 3 days in advance. Check sea conditions the morning of departure. Myrtos Beach has no shade — bring hats and reef-safe sunscreen. Melissani Lake visits are time-limited — aim for 10:00–12:00 when the sun illuminates the cave.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided scuba diving session in the waters around Navagio Beach — explore underwater rock formations, sea caves, and marine life with a certified PADI dive master. The waters around the Navagio coast are exceptionally clear with 20–30m visibility. Suitable for all levels including beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a luxurious afternoon. Enjoy the hotel's private clifftop terrace with a chilled bottle of Greek wine and a premium cheese and charcuterie board. Optional: book a couple's aromatherapy treatment at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private boat dinner experience — a luxury wooden caïque (traditional Greek boat) is chartered with a private chef and crew. Dine on deck under the stars as the boat anchors in a secluded cove near Navagio Beach.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — granola with local yogurt and honey, smoked salmon bagel, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Post-dive recovery lunch at the hotel — protein-rich spread of grilled chicken souvlaki wraps, fresh vegetables, hummus, and fresh watermelon
meals.dinner: Private boat dinner: freshly grilled seafood caught that day (squid, prawns, and sea bream), Greek salad with barrel-aged feta, warm village bread with olive oil, and baklava for dessert — accompanied by premium Greek wines and finishing with local tsipouro spirit

day_by_day.notes: Diving certification not required for the beginner session but participants must complete a brief medical questionnaire. The private boat dinner is the highlight of the trip — book well in advance and confirm weather conditions the day before. Bring a light layer as it can be cooler on the water after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — take one last swim at Navagio Beach via the hotel's private boat transfer. Soak in the iconic scenery and crystal-clear water one final time. Collect a few white pebbles as a memento (permitted in small quantities).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a farewell spa treatment — 2-hour 'Greek Ritual' package including olive oil body scrub, aromatic herb wrap, and a relaxing full-body massage. Pack and prepare for departure the following day.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the hotel's finest clifftop table — the hotel chef prepares a special farewell menu celebrating the best of Zakynthian cuisine. Sommelier presents a curated selection of the finest Greek wines tasted throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full premium spread, take your time and enjoy the last morning view from the terrace
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel pool — mezze selection of tzatziki, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, stuffed peppers, and fresh pita bread
meals.dinner: Farewell 6-course gala dinner: (1) Champagne and local oysters, (2) Grilled octopus with fava purée, (3) Prawn saganaki with tomato and feta, (4) Sorbet intermezzo with ouzo, (5) Slow-roasted Zakynthian lamb with herb-roasted potatoes and seasonal vegetables, (6) Dessert trio: loukoumades, galaktoboureko, and mandolato — paired with a premium selection of Greek wines and finishing with aged Metaxa 12-star brandy

day_by_day.notes: Ask the hotel concierge to arrange any last-minute premium gift purchases: local olive oil, honey, mandolato, and Zakynthian wine make excellent take-home gifts. Confirm airport transfer timing for the following morning. Tip the hotel staff and private boat crew appropriately — service throughout has been exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast on the private terrace with one last panoramic view of the Ionian Sea and Navagio Beach. Check out of the boutique hotel. Private luxury transfer to Zakynthos International Airport for departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Zakynthos. Carry memories of 13 extraordinary days of pristine beaches, world-class food, turquoise waters, and authentic Greek island luxury.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or upon return home.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — a leisurely full Greek spread: local yogurt with Zakynthian thyme honey, fresh pastries, eggs any style, local cheeses, cold cuts, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light snack at Zakynthos Airport or aboard the flight — the hotel can prepare a premium departure snack box with local treats for the journey
meals.dinner: In-flight or at home

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 11:00 — arrange a late check-out if your flight departs in the afternoon (subject to availability). Allow at least 2 hours before departure for the airport transfer from Navagio Beach area. Take a final photo from the clifftop viewpoint before leaving — it will be the image you remember most.
